title: Multi-Tenant Incident Simulation Framework
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document describes the Multi-Tenant Incident Simulation Framework (MTISF) — a standardized, reproducible suite for exercising platform failure modes that impact multiple tenants simultaneously. MTISF is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and oncall leads to validate isolation, SLO degradation profiles, cost-accounting signals, operational runbooks, and automated fallback logic before production rollouts.

Goals
- Provide a catalog of scenario templates that simulate realistic multi-tenant incidents (noisy neighbors, bursty cold-starts, KV cache collapse, model variant fallback storms, regional partition).
- Define a reproducible execution plan and tooling (simctl + k8s job templates) so simulations can be run in staging and restricted production *with safeguards*.
- Produce measurable validation criteria: SLO/SLIs, observability signals, billing/cost deltas, and tenant-impact reports.
- Capture artifacts for postmortems and continuous improvement (retro template, remediation backlog).

Scope and non-goals
- Scope: platform-level incidents affecting inference runtime, routing, caching, and tenancy economics. Includes both autonomous workload faults and control-plane misconfiguration simulations.
- Non-goals: model-level semantic evaluation (use Applied ML eval harness), long-running data-corruption scenarios (handled by data-ops).

Prerequisites
1. Target environment: staging or production namespace marked "chaos-enabled". Do not run MTISF in global prod without approvals.
2. simctl (internal synthetic traffic tool) v1.8+ installed on your workstation: https://internal-tools/simctl
3. A game day playbook ticket in JIRA with stakeholders listed and an approved blast-radius document.
4. Metrics dashboard template cloned: dashboards/mtisf-tenant-impact-2026.
5. SLO baseline snapshot taken within last 24 hours (use sloctl snapshot).

Roles and responsibilities
- Simulation Lead: coordinates the run, verifies prechecks, signs off for blast-radius. Typically a platform SRE.
- Sandbox Owner: ensures target namespace has resource quotas, network policies, and deletion protections in place.
- Metrics/Telemetry Owner: validates dashboards ingest simulation tags and metrics.
- Incident Commander (if escalation): follows standard incident process.

Safety guardrails
- Kill-switch: all simulations must be executed through the simctl controller which exposes an emergency abort endpoint: POST https://simctl.internal/abort?run_id=<id>. The run_id is printed at job start.
- Rate limits: synthetic traffic is capped by default to 25% of peak production RPS for staging, 5% for production.
- Tenant allowlist: by default simulations target synthetic tenants; any real tenant inclusion must be explicitly approved and recorded.
- Timebox: each scenario run must include an automatic teardown at T+30 minutes unless extended by Simulation Lead.

Scenario catalog (table)
| id | name | intent | primary signals to observe | blast-radius | notes |
| S-101 | Noisy-Neighbor CPU Flood | Assess fairness and eviction behavior under a tenant consuming 80% of host CPU | per-tenant cpuutil, queue depth, eviction events, p95 latency per-tenant | medium | Uses pod-level CPU burn on selected worker nodes |
| S-114 | KV Prefix Cache Collapse | Validate cache healing, cold-start latency, and cache stampede detection | KV hit-rate, p50/p95 token lat, burst cache regen errors | high | Requires temporary cache TTL override injection |
| S-122 | Model-Fallback Storm | Simulate primary model rollout failing and thousands of requests hitting fallback variants | model-fallback-rate, model-load-duration, token-cost-delta | high | Watch cost and token-accounting; may trigger billing alerts |
| S-135 | Regional Egress Partition | Validate routing fallback to other regions and cross-region SLOs | cross-region latency, routing-fanout, data residency markers | critical | Only to be run in limited-prod with executive approval |

Pre-run checklist (numbered)
1. Create a JIRA ticket with run template and notify #platform-gamedays 48 hours prior.
2. Confirm telemetry pusher and dashboards are active and sliced by run_id tag.
3. Snapshot SLOs: sloctl snapshot --name mtisf-<run_id>.
4. Apply resource quotas and cgroups limits to target namespace.
5. Validate kill-switch integration and test abort with a small dry-run.

Example execution (Noisy-Neighbor CPU Flood S-101)
1) Start run in simctl (from your laptop):

$ simctl run start --scenario S-101 --namespace chaos-staging --duration 00:30:00 --max-rps 400 --tag mtisf-run-20260310

Output: run_id=mtisf-run-20260310

2) Observe the synthesized traffic via dashboards: dashboards/mtisf-tenant-impact-2026?run_id=mtisf-run-20260310
3) If host CPU exceeds the safety threshold (85%), trigger automatic scale or abort. To abort:

$ curl -X POST "https://simctl.internal/abort?run_id=mtisf-run-20260310" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SIMCTL_TOKEN"

Kubernetes job template (example)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: mtisf-s101-worker
  labels:
    app: mtisf
    scenario: s-101
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: burner
        image: internal/synthetic-burner:stable
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: "4"
            memory: "8Gi"
        env:
        - name: TARGET_SERVICE
          value: "inference-gateway"
        - name: RUN_ID
          value: "mtisf-run-20260310"
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 1

Validation metrics and acceptance criteria
- Per-tenant p95 latency should not increase by > 3x baseline for more than 5 consecutive minutes.
- Error rate increase must remain < 0.5% absolute over baseline for synthetic tenants.
- Cache hit-rate should recover to > 80% of baseline within 10 minutes after induced collapse.
- Billing/cost delta for scenario should be < 20% of daily expected spend for the affected services.
- No customer-visible SLA breaches (customer-tagged tenants must be in allowlist).

Dashboards, alerts, and traces to watch
- mtisf/tenant-latency-by-tenant (p50/p95/p99 time series)
- mtisf/kv-hit-rate (live) with synthetic-tag filtering
- platform/cost-signal-fanout (per-service token-cost and token-rate)
- Alerts: MTISF::CPU-Safety (firing at node_cpu > 85%), MTISF::CrossRegionFallback (p50 increase > 300ms for 3m)

Post-run artifacts and evidence
- Exported dashboard snapshot (PNG + JSON).
- sloctl diff --from last_snapshot --to mtisf-<run_id> (output attached to JIRA).
- simctl run report --run_id <id> (includes per-tenant breakdown and raw traces).
- A short retro using the template section below.

Retrospective template (use in JIRA retro ticket)
1. Summary: 3-sentence incident summary and top-3 findings.
2. What happened: timeline with key events and timestamps.
3. Why it happened: root causes and contributing factors.
4. What we learned: gaps in tooling, dashboards, or runbook steps.
5. Action items: owner, priority, ETA.
6. Follow-ups: policy changes, automation tasks, and required PRs.

Common pitfalls and mitigation tips
- Pitfall: dashboards not ingesting run_id tags. Mitigation: pre-run telemetry smoke test: simctl run smoke --tag <run_id>.
- Pitfall: unintended customer impact. Mitigation: strict tenant allowlist and pre-run validation by Sandbox Owner.
- Pitfall: billing spike alarm storms. Mitigation: configure temporary noise suppression on billing alerts and annotate alerts with mtisf-run tag.

Automation and CI integration ideas
- Gate feature rollout by running a dry-run scenario S-122 (KV Prefix Cache Collapse) inside CI synthetic environment and failing the pipeline if acceptance criteria are not met.
- Integrate simctl with Slack for structured notifications (start/completion/abort) and attach run artifacts automatically.

Roadmap items (next 12 months)
- Add tenant-behavioral models to simctl so workload shapes better reflect top 20 customers. (Q2 2026)
- Add automated remediation playbooks that can be toggled as part of the run (auto-scale, eviction heuristics). (Q3 2026)
- Build a reproducible production-limited suite to run weekly on a rolling schedule for continuous validation. (Q4 2026)

Appendix: quick commands
- List running sims: simctl run list --state active
- Abort by run_id: simctl run abort --run_id mtisf-run-20260310
- Generate report: simctl run report --run_id mtisf-run-20260310 --format json > report.json
